claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if Meta publishes an erratum revising these production bandwidth or latency figures, or if a later primary disclosure shows the CXL tier reaching parity with local DRAM on bandwidth and latency for the same deployment.
claims.statement: Meta reports that the CXL-expanded memory it runs in production delivers roughly 10x lower bandwidth and roughly 60% higher latency than local memory; measured peak bandwidth is 48 GBps for CXL versus 497 GBps native on all-read traffic, and access latency at 60% bandwidth utilisation is 372 ns for CXL versus 234 ns native.

claims.disproof_condition: Downgrade if Meta later discloses that no workloads opt out of CXL capacity, or that expanded memory is enabled fleet-wide without per-workload exclusion.
claims.statement: Meta states that some workloads experience performance regressions on CXL-attached memory and are better served by opting out of CXL capacity, and that per-workload configuration automatically disables expanded memory for workloads that cannot tolerate the increased latency; the disclosed benefit is therefore capacity-bound and workload-selective rather than fleet-wide.
